title: Convert the scaffold to a Kotlin + Compose baseline
user_visible_behavior: The app launches and shows a single Compose screen with the project's dark theme background instead of the default Views layout.
verification: ./init.sh completes with no error
The app launches on a device or emulator and renders a Compose screen
No androidx.appcompat or com.google.android.material View dependency remains in app/build.gradle.kts
notes: The scaffold is a Views-based Android Studio template: no Kotlin plugin alias, no Compose, appcompat and Material Views only. This slice replaces that baseline. Keep it to build config plus one placeholder screen; theming proper belongs to design-tokens-theme.

title: Create the multi-module skeleton with :core modules
user_visible_behavior: The project builds with :app, :core:model, :core:ui and :core:data modules in place, and the app still launches.
verification: ./init.sh completes with no error
settings.gradle.kts includes every new module
The app still launches and renders its placeholder screen
notes: D-03. Feature modules are added by the slices that need them, not up front. No feature module may depend on another; shared contracts live in :core:* and binding happens in :app.

title: Enforce feature module isolation with Konsist
user_visible_behavior: A test fails when one feature module imports another, and passes on the current module layout.
verification: ./gradlew check runs the Konsist test and it passes
A deliberate cross-feature import makes the test fail, then is reverted
./init.sh reports konsist as wired
notes: D-03. The failing case must be demonstrated, not assumed: a rule that cannot fail proves nothing. Konsist output is course evidence and later proves the assistant did not reach into feature modules.

title: Wire detekt and ktlint into the check task
user_visible_behavior: ./gradlew check fails on a formatting or static-analysis violation and passes on clean code.
verification: ./gradlew check runs both tools and passes on the current tree
A deliberate violation fails the gate, then is reverted
./init.sh reports detekt and ktlint as wired
notes: Keep the gate fast; feature-flow runs init.sh on every validation.

title: Set up the composable presenter pattern with a Molecule test
user_visible_behavior: A sample presenter emits a UiModel and is covered by a unit test that runs on the JVM without an Android device.
verification: ./gradlew check runs the presenter test on the JVM with no emulator
The test asserts at least one state transition, not just a first emission
notes: D-02, no ViewModels. Two known traps in the reference pattern, both documented in the bitácora section 3.5: hashCode derived from handle while equals compared key, breaking the contract, and the invoke operator used without being declared. Do not reintroduce either.

title: Implement the dark theme and design tokens
user_visible_behavior: Every screen uses the project's dark palette and type scale; no light theme exists.
verification: A Compose preview renders the palette and type scale
Amber is exposed as a semantic accent, not applied as generic decoration
Contrast of amber-on-background and muted-text-on-surface is measured and recorded
notes: Tokens are in DESIGN.md. The hex values there are derived from the written direction, not measured from the original mockup: open question recorded in risks-and-open-questions.md. Dark only, no light variant (D-12 for copy language).

title: Define the domain types in :core:model
user_visible_behavior: Jam, JamSong, Slot and Song exist as Kotlin types with their states, and unit tests cover slot-open and lineup rules.
verification: ./gradlew check runs the domain tests and they pass
A Slot with no musician reports as open and one with a musician does not
Jam status models DRAFT and PUBLISHED only
notes: docs/domain-model.md. Archived is not a stored status: a jam is historical when its date has passed. There is no Musician entity; a musician is a name on a Slot (D-05). The key lives on JamSong, not Song (D-08).

title: Define the Sheet schema and document it
user_visible_behavior: The catalog, jams and assignments tabs exist in the Sheet with agreed columns, and the schema is written down in the repo.
verification: Every domain type maps to columns with no ambiguity about identifiers
A handful of real songs are loaded and read back correctly by hand
The schema is committed as documentation
notes: TOP BLOCKER, recorded in risks-and-open-questions.md. Blocked on a human decision, not on code. It gates every repository slice and, separately, gates the assistant: week 5 needs real repertoire loaded, and a twelve-song catalog cannot produce an interesting themed setlist. Load repertoire in parallel with development.

title: Expose a read endpoint for the song catalog
user_visible_behavior: A GET request to the Apps Script deployment returns the song catalog as JSON.
verification: The deployed URL returns catalog JSON matching the schema
A song with missing optional enrichment fields still serializes correctly
notes: D-04: Sheet to app, read-only. Measure and record response latency here; it informs the optimistic-update decision on the write side.

title: Read the catalog into a Room cache
user_visible_behavior: The app fetches the catalog once, stores it locally, and serves songs from the cache when offline.
verification: A unit test covers the repository mapping from JSON to domain types
With the network disabled the cached catalog is still returned
Cache staleness is exposed so the UI can indicate it
notes: docs/technical-discovery.md. Offline reads are a requirement; the app shows last-known data with a staleness indicator rather than an error.

title: Show the next jam setlist collapsed
user_visible_behavior: A musician opens the app and sees the next jam's date, venue and its songs in collapsed rows showing position, title and key.
verification: A presenter test asserts the list state for a published jam
The key is visible in the collapsed row
The header shows time remaining in natural language
notes: The most important screen in the app, opened 90% of the time. The instrument strip is a separate slice because it is the component the screen depends on and deserves its own verification.

title: Add the instrument strip to each song row
user_visible_behavior: Each collapsed row shows one small icon per instrument in that song's lineup, distinguishing open slots from filled ones without expanding the row.
verification: A Compose preview covers an all-open, an all-filled and a mixed lineup
Open and filled remain distinguishable with color and luminance removed
Each icon carries a content description
notes: D-07, the component that makes the collapsed list useful. Dimmed means open, lit means filled. Brightness alone fails in glare and for low-vision users, in the dark bar this app targets: pair it with shape or fill. Open design question in risks-and-open-questions.md. Icons at roughly 16dp must be sourced or drawn first.

title: Expand a song row in place
user_visible_behavior: Tapping a row expands it to show the artist, then open slots first, then filled slots with musician names. Several rows can be expanded at once.
verification: A presenter test asserts open slots are ordered before filled ones
Two rows can be expanded simultaneously
Expanding does not displace the rest of the list disorientingly
notes: Actionable content on top. bb-blues-jam-design-prompt.md section 1.

title: Filter the setlist by instrument with an open slot
user_visible_behavior: Tapping an instrument chip shows only songs with an open slot for it, with a count of matching songs and a way to clear the filter.
verification: A presenter test covers filtering for each of the six instruments
The no-results case is distinct from the empty case and names the active filter
Clearing the filter restores the full list
notes: D-06, D-07. Answers the musician's primary question. A song with no open slots is excluded while a filter is active but still listed otherwise.

title: Implement the loading, empty, error and offline states
user_visible_behavior: Each non-happy path renders its own treatment: skeleton rows while loading, a concrete invitation when empty, a retry button on error, and cached data with a staleness indicator when offline.
verification: A Compose preview covers all four states
Loading uses skeleton rows, not a centered spinner
The offline state shows data with a staleness indicator rather than an error
notes: DESIGN.md. Kept as one slice deliberately: the four states are branches of a single presenter surface and are verified by one preview file, so splitting them would create management overhead without adding verification. The unpublished-setlist case is a separate slice because it is a product state rather than a failure state, and must not look like the empty state.

title: Hide a draft setlist from musicians
user_visible_behavior: While a jam is in draft, a musician sees the date and venue plus a message that the list is being assembled, and no songs.
verification: A presenter test asserts no songs are exposed for a DRAFT jam
The message is visibly distinct from the empty state
The read endpoint does not serve draft songs to an unauthenticated client
notes: Hiding in the UI is not sufficient; the data should not reach an unauthenticated client at all. Recorded in docs/user-and-access-model.md.

title: Show the song detail screen
user_visible_behavior: Opening a song shows its title, artist, the key displayed very large, its tags, tempo when present, and the full lineup grouped by instrument.
verification: A Compose preview renders a song with and without optional enrichment fields
The key is the largest element on the screen
A song with no artwork, tempo or tags still renders correctly
notes: Every enrichment field is optional and may be permanently absent; that is not an error state (D-09).

title: Open the guitar tab in the browser
user_visible_behavior: A song with a stored songsterrId shows a button that opens its tab in the browser; a song without one shows no button.
verification: The button opens the correct external URL
The button is absent when songsterrId is null
notes: D-10. No in-app rendering. Songsterr has no official API, so this must degrade silently.

title: List past jams in reverse chronological order
user_visible_behavior: The Anteriores tab shows past jams newest first, each with date, venue, song count and the first few titles.
verification: A presenter test asserts reverse chronological ordering
The archive treatment is muted, with amber reserved for keys
The empty state renders when there is no history
notes: D-04: past jams are read-only, Sheet is their authority.

title: Show a past jam read-only
user_visible_behavior: Opening a past jam shows its setlist with keys and who played, with no filter and no notion of open slots.
verification: No admin control and no filter appears, even when logged in as admin
Slots render as filled with no open-slot affordance
notes: Editing history is not supported. Recorded in docs/user-and-access-model.md.

title: Show the info screen
user_visible_behavior: The Info tab explains what the jam is, where and when it happens, how to join, links to social media, and offers a discreet admin entry point.
verification: Every link opens correctly
The admin entry point is present but discreet
Copy is in Rioplatense Spanish using vos
notes: D-12. This slice has no backend dependency and can run early if the Sheet stays blocked.

title: Wire the three tabs into bottom navigation
user_visible_behavior: The user moves between Próxima jam, Anteriores and Info, and each tab keeps its scroll position.
verification: Switching tabs preserves each tab's state
Binding happens in :app with no feature-to-feature dependency
Konsist still passes
notes: D-03: :app is where features are bound together.

title: Log in as admin with a passphrase
user_visible_behavior: Entering the correct passphrase reveals admin controls; entering a wrong one shows an error and reveals nothing.
verification: A correct passphrase sets the local admin flag and a wrong one does not
The flag survives an app restart
The error state renders as designed
notes: D-11. No Firebase Auth, no OAuth, no accounts. A visible logout belongs on the info screen. The local flag only draws controls; it authorizes nothing.

title: Validate the passphrase on every write endpoint
user_visible_behavior: A write request without a valid passphrase is rejected by Apps Script, regardless of what the client believes.
verification: A write with no passphrase is rejected
A write with a stale passphrase after rotation is rejected
A valid write succeeds
notes: The Apps Script URL is reachable directly, so this is the only real access control in the product. Rotating the passphrase in the Sheet is the revocation mechanism. A rejected write after rotation must read as access changed, not as a generic network error.

title: Add a song from the catalog to the setlist
user_visible_behavior: The admin picks a song from the catalog and it appears in the upcoming setlist, persisted to the Sheet.
verification: The song appears locally and is present in the Sheet after a reload
The mutation is a repository function, not UI-only logic
A failed write surfaces visibly and does not leave a phantom row
notes: D-13: the first mutation, so it sets the pattern for every later one. Apps Script latency is expected; optimistic state with later confirmation, and a real rollback path.

title: Remove a song from the setlist
user_visible_behavior: The admin removes a song from the upcoming setlist and the change persists to the Sheet.
verification: The song disappears locally and is gone from the Sheet after a reload
Removing a song does not affect the catalog entry

title: Set the key on a scheduled song
user_visible_behavior: The admin sets the key for a song in the setlist, and musicians see it on the collapsed row.
verification: The key persists to the Sheet
The catalog song's defaultKey is left untouched
The change is visible on a published jam immediately
notes: D-08, D-13. The key belongs to the JamSong, not to the Song: that distinction is the whole reason the two types are separate.

title: Adjust a song's lineup
user_visible_behavior: The admin changes how many slots of each instrument a song needs, and the instrument strip updates.
verification: A lineup change persists to the Sheet
A lineup with zero slots of an instrument is valid and renders correctly
Removing a slot that holds a musician is handled deliberately, not silently
notes: D-06. Default is 2 guitars, bass, drums, vocals, harmonica, keyboards.

title: Assign a musician to an open slot
user_visible_behavior: The admin taps an open slot, types a name with suggestions from musicians who played before, and the slot becomes filled.
verification: The assignment persists to the Sheet
The instrument is fixed by the slot and is not selectable
Suggestions come from prior jams
notes: D-05: only the admin assigns. Where suggestions come from depends on the Sheet schema, recorded as an open question. Two musicians sharing a name are not disambiguated, by design.

title: Clear a filled slot
user_visible_behavior: The admin removes a musician from a slot and it returns to open.
verification: The slot returns to open locally and in the Sheet
The instrument strip and any active filter update accordingly
notes: D-13. Completes the assign/clear pair; there is no reserved intermediate state.

title: Reorder songs in the setlist
user_visible_behavior: The admin changes a song's position and the new order persists for everyone.
verification: The new order persists to the Sheet
Positions stay contiguous with no gaps or duplicates
The reorder affordance meets the 48dp touch target minimum
notes: D-13. Drag-to-reorder versus explicit move actions is an open design question: dragging conflicts with 48dp targets on a dense one-handed list.

title: Publish the setlist
user_visible_behavior: The admin publishes a draft jam, the badge changes from Borrador to Publicada, and musicians can now see the songs.
verification: The status persists to the Sheet and musicians see the setlist
A failed publish is unmissable and does not report success
The write failure is logged locally
notes: D-13, and the highest-stakes mutation in the product. A silently failed publish means the admin believes the list is live while musicians read something stale: the worst outcome this app can produce. Optimistic state is not acceptable here without explicit confirmation.

title: Register every mutation in one action contract
user_visible_behavior: Every admin mutation is reachable through a single registry of repository functions, verified to be complete against the documented list.
verification: All eight mutations are registered: add song, remove song, set key, adjust lineup, assign musician, clear slot, reorder, publish
A test asserts no mutation exists only in the UI layer
Konsist confirms the registry lives in :app and no feature module depends on another
notes: D-13, the slice the whole phase 2 assistant rests on. Confirm the mutation list is complete before this runs; it is an open question in risks-and-open-questions.md. Capture the feature-module diff here: proving the assistant was added without touching feature modules is course evidence.

title: Enrich songs from music APIs in the background
user_visible_behavior: After a song is added, its artwork and canonical metadata appear once fetched, and nothing blocks if the fetch never succeeds.
verification: Enrichment runs on song add, never during list rendering
MusicBrainz requests stay within 1 req/s
With every API unreachable, the app remains fully usable
notes: D-09. MusicBrainz for identity and artistArea, Deezer for artwork and preview, Last.fm for similar artists. artistArea is what lets blues nacional argentino be filtered by data rather than by model memory, which matters for D-14. Fully removable if the timeline tightens.
